text: The following question stood in the name of Mr Desmond Choo – 9 To ask the Minister for Defence (a) whether the Houthis' attacks on shipping in the Red Sea impacts Singapore's maritime security; and (b) noting that the US and other nations have announced the creation of a multinational maritime security initiative to secure the Red Sea, whether the SAF will be contributing to this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is a major Sea Line of Communications (SLOC) with approximately 12% of global trade by volume and 30% of global container traffic.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: There have been 20 such attacks, including one on a Singapore-flagged vessel MAERSK Hangzhou.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As a result, all five of the world's largest global shipping companies, namely the Mediterranean Shipping Company, Maersk, CMA CGM, COSCO, Hapag-Lloyd and other shipping lines, had earlier announced that they would suspend transits through the Red Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Prior to the attacks, around 60 ships passed through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea daily, but the number has dropped by about a third in recent weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore-registered ships have also been affected, with the number of daily transits through the Red Sea now approximately halved.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The disruption of the Red Sea SLOC will have an impact on global supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: However, based on the current situation, the immediate impact on Singapore is expected to be limited, as the majority of our critical supplies, such as food and pharmaceuticals, are delivered via air freight or do not pass through the Red Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our local manufacturers also seem to have sufficient spare inventory to hedge against supply disruptions, though they are worried about increases in business costs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Nonetheless, it is in our interest for Singapore to join cause with the international community to protect and ensure that key SLOCs around the world remain open, especially if threatened by unlawful acts by non-state actors or terrorist groups.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have previously articulated key principles that govern the Straits of Malacca and Singapore when this key SLOC was threatened by piracy and sea robbery.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think some Members would remember those incidents, that resulted in insurance premiums for ships that traverse the Straits of Malacca and Singapore to increase manyfold.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These principles were articulated in the 2005 Shangri-La Dialogue.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: First, the primary responsibility of maritime security lies with the littoral states.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Second, the international community and agencies, such as the International Maritime Organization (IMO), have a role to play.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Third, all measures have to be in accordance with international law and respect the sovereignty of the littoral states.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As Mr Desmond Choo mentioned, the United States has announced the launch of the multinational Operation Prosperity Guardian to ensure maritime security in the Red Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This operation aligns with the key principles that I have just articulated.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In this regard, Singapore hopes that the littoral states that surround the Red Sea step up efforts to end the unlawful Houthi attacks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The international community of user states also has a role to play.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In particular, there is the 39-nation Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), of which Singapore has been a member since 2009.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The CMF's Combined Task Force (CTF) 153: Red Sea Maritime Security has been tasked to keep the Red Sea SLOC open and safe.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The launch of Operation Prosperity Guardian aims to restore international confidence and the free flow of maritime shipping through the area.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) had similarly participated in the Combined Task Force 151.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: That was a counter piracy effort in the Gulf of Aden, where we deployed assets for quite a long time from 2009 to 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Separately, Singapore and the SAF, together with our international partners, have continued to monitor developments in the region, including the ongoing need for humanitarian assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Some of you will remember that the SAF has been supporting Singapore's humanitarian contributions to Gaza and we were doing this through our Changi Regional Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Coordination Centre's information, networks and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Most recently, the SAF delivered relief supplies on 30 November last year to the Egyptian Red Crescent.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Further to this effort, the French Armed Forces has invited the SAF to provide two medical personnel to serve on FS Dixmude, now docked at the El-Arish port in Egypt.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is a reconfigured hospital ship and has been treating casualties from Gaza.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Does he also foresee that if the situation does not improve or the tension at the Red Sea escalates, that Singapore will also similarly increase our support to international task forces or supporting humanitarian support in the area?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I do not want to pre-empt the situation, it is a complex situation.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I would just make two general points and then perhaps a specific one.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In other words, it is focused primarily on keeping key sea lines of communication free, which is in our interest because if the same thing happens, as it did in the Straits of Malacca, we would want the international community for assistance as well, if that was necessary.
If the problem gets worse, we will assess it.
